name: Poppin Soda
description: My senior project at BYU-I, Poppin Soda is a mock soda company website built to learn React from scratch. Before starting, I completed a Udemy course to get up to speed, then applied that knowledge by building features like a shopping cart modal and a review section using Material UI. Since completing the course, I have returned to refine the project by migrating it to Vite and adding PropTypes for improved type safety. The site is currently live and open to explore.

name: RouteScout
description: A multi-step road trip planning wizard built with React, TypeScript, and the Google Maps Platform. Users enter a start and destination, choose from up to four route options, select interests from 15 categories, and receive suggested stops plotted on an interactive map. Stops can be filtered by rating, price, and distance, then reordered via drag-and-drop with live mileage and drive time updates. Completed trips can be exported to Google Maps or Apple Maps, downloaded as a GPX file, or shared via a read-only link. The app is backed by a Node/Express REST API with MongoDB, deployed on Render, and uses React Context with useReducer for state management.

name: Style Stage
description: A team project built around the challenge of restyling a web page using only CSS — no HTML changes, no JavaScript. I was responsible for the header, footer, navigation bar, the bottom card section, and various buttons throughout the page. The project deepened my understanding of CSS selectors, layout tools like Flexbox and Grid, and translating design concepts into code.

name: BYUI Rebuild
description: A pixel-faithful recreation of the BYU-I homepage as it appeared in April 2023, built without JavaScript. Using official BYU-I fonts, colors, icons, and content, the project focused on semantic HTML structure and precise CSS styling. The header and footer were simplified due to time constraints.

name: Weather App
description: A five-day weather forecast app for three cities, built to practice core JavaScript concepts including API data fetching, local storage, and working with JavaScript objects.

name: PHP Motors
description: A mock car dealership website built with PHP following the MVC architecture. Features include browsing vehicle listings, user authentication, and a vehicle search. Data is persisted using a relational MySQL database.

name: Chess
description: A fully functional chess program built as a team project in C++. The game follows all standard rules of chess, including special moves such as castling, en passant, and pawn promotion. Third-party Interact and OpenGL classes provided by BYU-I professor James Helfrich were used for rendering; all game logic was written by the team.

name: Orbit Simulator
description: A satellite orbit simulation built in C++ where players pilot a ship and destroy debris before it damages other satellites. Orbital physics are approximated using basic algebra and geometry, producing a visually convincing result.

name: C# ATM
description: A two-week self-directed sprint to learn C# fundamentals. The project simulates a basic ATM in the console, covering classes, control flow, loops, and list containers. Following the sprint, I completed two Udemy courses to further solidify my understanding of the language.
